sentences.text: Here’s how the vessel categories fit together.
An uninspected passenger vessel carries no more than six passengers for hire, and the operator needs at least an OUPV.
An inspected small passenger vessel carries more than six, up to the number on her Certificate of Inspection, and she needs a Master.
The third row is where captains get into trouble: the bareboat charter, also called a demise charter.
In a real one, the charterer hires the boat and supplies his own captain, and the owner steps away completely.
Why does that matter to you?
Because fake bareboat charters are a classic way to dodge the six-passenger limit, and the Coast Guard fines operators for them regularly.
If someone offers you a job running twelve people on an uninspected boat under a bareboat agreement, be very careful.
